domains.name: Cognition and how you feel
domains.why_space: NASA's Human Research Program names isolation and confinement as one of the five hazards of human spaceflight. Here you see your Decode result and your own alertness rating side by side, so you can follow your plan and decide when to request a review.
domains.limits_note: A 90-second task and a self-rating cannot tell you why you feel the way you do, and they are not a psychological assessment. They use different scales and are never combined into one number.
domains.how_to_measure: Once a day: rate your alertness from 1 to 10, note your mood, then play one 90-second Decode round.
domains.when_to_involve_specialist: Whenever a follow-up asks for a review, or any time you want one. Use Request help.
domains.risk: Risk of Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders

domains.name: Sleep and daily rhythm
domains.why_space: NASA's Human Research Program lists inadequate sleep and irregular schedules as a risk of human spaceflight. This card keeps your recorded sleep apart from the rest opportunity in your schedule, so you can follow your plan and review schedule conflicts and alternatives.
domains.limits_note: Recorded sleep is an estimate from your wrist sensor. Shorter sleep and a lower Decode result on the same days are two observations that happen together, not evidence that one causes the other.
domains.how_to_measure: Imported each morning from your wrist sensor, with its source. If last night's reading is missing, you can check the sensor or add the reading by hand.
domains.when_to_involve_specialist: When short recorded sleep continues after your plan steps, or when you want help with your schedule. Use Request help.
domains.risk: Risk from Inadequate Sleep and Irregular Schedules

domains.name: Heart and circulation
domains.why_space: Gravity fields are one of the five hazards of human spaceflight named by NASA, and NASA's list of spaceflight risks includes cardiovascular adaptations. Here you follow your resting pulse against your own reference and can request a review whenever you need one.
domains.limits_note: Resting pulse alone does not assess your heart health. A change from your reference is an observation, not an explanation.
domains.how_to_measure: Once a day, seated and at rest, with the wrist sensor in firm contact.
domains.when_to_involve_specialist: When your plan's review condition is met, or whenever you notice a symptom. Use Report something or Request help.
domains.review_status: TODO(review: the measuring conditions (seated, at rest, firm contact) need a source; lib:nasa-standard-measures is the closest existing id. Check the risk title against the HRP risk list.)

domains.name: Symptoms and temperature
domains.why_space: NASA's list of spaceflight risks includes altered immune system responses. This card keeps your reports in the order you made them, helps you fill in missing information and supports follow-up with the medical team.
domains.limits_note: Temperature is not an immunity score, and skin temperature is not core body temperature. A report is your own description; the medical team decides what it means.
domains.how_to_measure: Use Report something at any time. You do not need to choose a medical category.
domains.when_to_involve_specialist: You can send any symptom for review. This path never waits for a Decode result.
